one question in the rubric, such as whether a pillar appears
a standard size measure for the difference between two proportions

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and usage notes
sections.what: Explains the usage and what the harness may write, then imports the database, corpus builder, runner, validator and parameters.
sections.why: Sets the expectation that results are read-only except for one log entry.
sections.watch_out: The header's read-only promise should be checked again if the runner is changed.

sections.name: arg, pctOf, pts
sections.title: Flag and percentage helpers
sections.what: Reads a named command-line option with a default, and formats fractions as percentages and differences as percentage points, showing n/a for missing values.
sections.watch_out: A missing value prints n/a rather than zero, so an empty result is not mistaken for a rate of zero.

sections.name: storedOutcomeSplit
sections.title: Cross-check against the stored deck run
sections.what: Finds the latest succeeded deck run for an industry and reads its outcome split, so the harness's own grouping can be compared with it.
sections.why: Lets the owner see whether the harness groups outcomes the same way the real deck does.
sections.watch_out: If no run is stored, the cross-check is skipped and the report says so.

sections.name: printReport
sections.title: Printing the verdict table
sections.what: Prints one line per criterion showing outcome counts, rates, effect size, confidence range, p-value, required sample size and verdict, then a detail line for each.
sections.why: Fits a dense statistical result into one readable table.
sections.watch_out: Criterion names are cut at 48 characters, so long names are shortened on screen.

sections.name: main (part 1)
sections.title: Running both definitions per industry
sections.what: For each industry, builds the corpus, prints counts and pillars, prints outcome group sizes, runs the cross-check, runs the presence and salience definitions, prints each report, and then counts the stored records.
sections.why: The header places group sizes first because they limit how far each verdict can be trusted.
sections.watch_out: Small or empty outcome groups make verdicts unreliable, so check the group sizes before reading any verdict.

sections.name: main: if
sections.title: Optional JSON output
sections.what: If a JSON path was given, writes all the reports to that file and then exits.
sections.why: Lets the results be saved and compared later.
sections.watch_out: The script exits right after writing, so nothing that follows runs.

summary: A measurement harness that checks whether the scoring rubric's criteria actually separate projects that overran their schedules from those that delivered, for chosen industries, and prints the results.
purpose: Test the rubric on real data before anyone relies on its verdicts.
why: The header says the harness routes facts through the shipped framework and measures the result, leaving clustering, naming and the deck untouched.
how: For each industry, the script builds a corpus of routed facts, prints counts and pillars, and checks the outcome group sizes. It cross-checks outcome counts against the latest stored deck run. Then it runs two definitions, presence and salience, prints a verdict table for each, and optionally saves all reports to a JSON file. Finally it counts computation records for this engine.
inputs: Command-line options for industries and a JSON output path, with a default of lithium-mining and gas-power. Database contents and fixed rubric parameters.
outputs: A console report for each industry and definition. An optional JSON file. A count of computation records for this engine, which the header says is the only write.
risks: Small groups or many unknown cells can make verdicts unreliable. The header's claim that only the computation record is written should be re-checked if the runner changes.
debug: If an industry shows little data, read the corpus line for routed and unrouted facts. If the cross-check says no stored run, no completed deck run exists. If verdicts say refused, read the refusal reason on that line.
